actual_scope: For the fixed five-source word B0 B1 B0 B1 B2 B3 B4 B2 B4 B3 over F2, with source 3 entering in direction (1,1), the other sources entering in (1,0), paired readouts using covectors (1,0) and (1,1), and only the two paid row-shear generators, determine the exact minimum number of full-row XORs over every boundary-pair assignment that covers all 31 nonzero output masks.

This follows that package’s explicit open question about alternative boundary pairs and fixes its source word and operation model. The result is an exact minimum in that finite interface, not another alphabet extension or a supplier-level claim.

bottleneck_link: Frame changes are the charged interface overhead that can erase the predecessor’s two-child saving. Proving the minimum for every boundary choice decides whether readout retiming alone can reduce that term.
stop_rule: Stop after exact enumeration of all 4,194,304 boundary/projection demand sets and the exact six-frame transition dynamic program for every set that covers all 31 masks. Do not expand to other source words or infer selected-supplier profitability.
evidence: The exact finite search finds 848 covering demand sets. Their minimum frame-XOR cost histogram is 10:38, 12:248, 14:386, 16:176. The retained predecessor schedule is independently replayed at 10 XORs, so the minimum in this fixed model is exactly 10. This is not a lower bound for other source paths or a complete supplier cost.
